newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude chartists cautiously bullish.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude chartists cautiously bullish.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ June NYMEX crude faces resistance at $21.50-$21.55 and support at $20.85-90.
+ Heating oil needs to overcome March 19's high of 57.45 cents while gasoline faces resistance at 65.20.

NYMEX crude oil and refined products futures were expected to gain strength on Friday although traders and technical analysts were cautious about whether markets have enough energy to punch through resistance.
June NYMEX crude closed nine cents a barrel weaker on Thursday at $21.30 while June gasoline was 0.34 cents weaker at 64.04 cents and June heating oil was 0.06 cents firmer at 56.48.

MeesPierson Derivatives in London said of energy futures markets: "after a day of consolidating recent gains we now need momentum if we are to continue the uptrend. We feel that failure to improve today would lead to a gentle erosion of prices."
Claudia LaCovey at Analytics Research Corp. in Bethesda, Maryland, said of June crude: "We have been bumping into our strong resistance level at $21.50."
"We have a short term down move (from January) and a little up move and it is a battle to see which one takes control," she said, basing her analysis on her company's proprietary chart technique.

She pegged higher resistance at $21.73 and "key resistance" at $22.01. "If it exceeds this ($22.01) within 20 or 30 cents then the short term down move from the swing high in January will have been broken."
For Friday's session she said she would be "shorting at the highs of $21.50-$21.55, with a reversal above that, but I would prefer to play from the long side with support at $20.89."
Above this lies more support at $21.19 and $21.34, she added.
MeesPierson expected June crude to trade within "a nicely defined range" between $21.16/$21.18 and $21.42/44."
LaCovey was optimistic about heating oil and set a target of 57.45 cents a gallon, the high on March 19.
"It looks like it is definitely moving out of this short term down move from January," she said.
"It has set a nice swing low (at 52.20) and it looks like we will be playing from the long side, looking to break out above 57.45."
The contract would find support at 55.45 and 55.78, she said.
Gasoline would encounter resistance at 65.20 cents a gallon and then 67.50, while support would weigh in at 63.82, then at 63.58 and 62.82.
